description: 12-segment expert-coded transcript: student wellbeing during remote study. expert_codes are the human reference; model_codes are the recorded (cassette) model output used for replay.

segments.text: When the university moved everything online, I lost my whole routine overnight.
I stopped going to bed at a reasonable hour because there was no reason to get up.
Honestly, I think the online lectures were just as good, maybe even better for reviewing.
But you lose the corridor conversations, and that is where the real learning happened.
The university kept saying we were 'all in this together', which felt hollow to me.
Students are expected to just manage everything themselves now, as if we asked for this.
I started studying with a friend over video calls, and that held me together.
My grades actually went up, though I cannot say I learned more.
Interviewer: How did the exams change?
They became open-book, which rewarded people who were good at finding things fast.
In a way the pandemic exposed how fragile our support systems always were.
I suppose we adapted, but I would not want to do it again.
